fields.objective: high-level intent text (owner or upstream lane)
fields.needs: tuple of normalized need ids (see need_vocabulary)
fields.success_criteria: tuple of strings (carried into contract verification criteria)

resolution_contract.workflow: {recipe_id, recipe_version, params} bound through declared recipe bind roles
resolution_contract.gap: durable fabric.gap.recorded record with needed_action + intent lineage

capability_resolution_contract.authority: existing Fabric catalog + recipe registry (no second registry)
recipe_declarations_added: Recipe.needs (normalized need ids the recipe satisfies)
RecipeParameter.bind (input role bound into that parameter)
capability_resolution_contract.readiness: Fabric catalog spec presence + observed readiness; the verified capability is then bound to the mission resource through the canonical capability.state_changed event
capability_resolution_contract.determinism: candidate set = recipes whose declared needs cover the intent; rank = smallest extra-need footprint, then recipe id

verification_contract.rule: A deterministic effect the runtime can re-derive is certified by the runtime's own predicate. A model verdict may never authorize such a step, and a model PASS that is not backed by a JARVIS-owned artifact predicate is still refused.
verification_contract.seam: mission verifier session -> fabric.adapter.try_fabric_dispatch (role=verifier) -> fabric.adapter.canonical_verifier_dispatch -> fabric.loop.canonical_predicate_verdict over the step's recorded fabric.spine.result receipt
declines_to_the_model_path_when: the mission step's contract capability does not resolve to a Fabric action kind
the step has no recorded fabric.spine.result receipt
the recorded observation is empty or malformed
the recorded subject (path/target/source_ref/worktree) diverges from the declared intent payload
recorded_facts: verdict evidence carries jarvis_predicate + verifier_answered_by (the frozen binding names the routed provider and is captured before the session)
event fabric.canonical_verification_observed (mission_id, step_id, run_id, action_kind, capability_id, predicate, reverified, receipt_id, effect_id, subject_ref, declared)
fail_closed: re-derivation is from reality (artifact replay or the action verifier over the recorded observation); the receipt's own verified/success fields are never trusted
MISMATCH is reported as FAIL, never softened
a resumed pass whose frozen binding drifted is refused with BLOCKED and the ledger's own reason instead of raising EventConflict out of the loop
fabrication_risks: Trust boundary (pre-existing product model, deliberately unchanged): the event ledger is authoritative, so an actor able to append arbitrary fabric.spine.result receipts could obtain a certification whose observation matches reality. The re-derivation validates the observation against the filesystem, not against who wrote the event; models do not author fabric.spine.result.

The declared-vs-observed subject guard compares the subject refs a contract declares (path/target/source_ref/worktree); a contract that declares its subject under none of those keys is certified purely on the predicate's re-derivation.

outcome_contract.unrealizable_intent: plan step FAILED + mission BLOCKED + portfolio.intent_unresolved (durable) + Executive bounded retry owns the resume
outcome_contract.duplicate_guarantees: effect journal keys per (mission, step, attempt); identical re-delivery dedupes, changed payload records

events_added_or_changed: portfolio.intent_unresolved (NEW, inert additive record: decision_id, item_id, mission_id, intent_id, intent_needs, gap, missing_inputs, reason)
fabric.canonical_verification_observed (NEW, inert additive record: the runtime predicate's re-derived verdict for a mission step, with effect/receipt/subject lineage)
capability.state_changed (existing event now also emitted by the intent-resolution capability binding and by the one-time registered-resource readiness projection)
executive.plan_updated (existing event now also emitted by _record_unrealizable_intent with the missing cap.* requirements attached)
files_likely_to_conflict: src/jarvis_foundry/executive/autonomy.py (intent travels with the work item; registered-resource capability projection in run_autonomy_cycle)
src/jarvis_foundry/mission/loop.py (acceptance predicate + binding-drift refusal in run_step)
requirements_from_lane_a: Deliver the selected mission's intent in the normalized contract above (objective + needs + role inputs) instead of naming a recipe or building recipe params; either in objective metadata['intent'] or through an equivalent public call.
Do not carry execution internals (browser/UIA/git) into owner-level goals: express the requirement as normalized needs only.
If the chosen mission needs inputs the runtime cannot supply, declare them in the intent inputs so the runtime can BLOCK honestly and list exactly what is missing.

Do not assume a model verdict can authorize a deterministic step: the runtime certifies those with its own predicate, and the verifier session for such a step is answered by the Fabric rather than by the routed provider.
guarantees_to_lane_a: A selected objective/mission with a normalized intent gets a deterministic capability/workflow resolution with recorded provenance (considered candidates, chosen recipe, bound params).

Unrealizable intents produce a durable gap plus an honest blocked materialization; the objective is left resumable through the Executive's bounded retry path (no silent prose fallback, no stranded mission).
Workflow execution reports nested receipts; effect identity/exactly-once semantics are unchanged and remain owned by effects.py.
Registered resources have their declared capability readiness projected once into the durable capability plane, so selection no longer depends on a developer-side control step.

A mission step whose capability resolves to a Fabric action kind is verified by the runtime's own predicate over the recorded receipt, so a deterministic effect can reach PASSED without any provider being asked to judge it; the verdict records both the routed provider and who actually answered.

A verification pass that is resumed after the frozen state drifted refuses honestly (BLOCKED + the ledger's reason) instead of raising a control-plane exception, and stays resumable through a fresh attempt.
semantic_decisions: Recipe selection is data-driven (declared needs), never LLM-judged: the resolver is a binder, not a planner.
The need vocabulary is the owner-level seam; action kinds, capabilities and recipe ids stay runtime-internal.
Missing capability -> durable gap + bounded retry; missing supplied inputs -> BLOCKED with the exact missing roles (never a guess).
Capability binding for a mission records capability.state_changed once per (resource, capability); per-mission lineage lives in the contract provenance.

Verification precedence: the runtime's own predicate for anything it can re-derive; a model only for judgment steps. The acceptance rule that demands a JARVIS-owned artifact predicate is unchanged and still refuses an unbacked model PASS.
open_gaps: Native Windows toast remains unproven (winotify backend not installed); in-app toast is proven.
Real GitHub API writes and third-party authenticated sites remain live-only (owner-authorized config absent in this lane).
Gap-bridge wake ownership of intent-resolution gaps is partial (the requirement is attached and durable; the bridge wake -> replan path was not exercised end-to-end).
Lane-A semantic convergence: the parallel lane must deliver intents in the published shape before the two lanes converge.
